slots.brief: Body cools from one temperature range to another in a given time; using Newton's law of cooling, find the time for a second (stated) temperature drop in the same surroundings.
Projectile launched from ground with given speed and angle; find a standard quantity such as time of flight or horizontal range using two suvat equations.
Radioactive sample with given half-life decays for a stated multiple of the half-life; find the fraction of the sample remaining (or nuclei disintegrated).
Given a spring–mass SHM with stated amplitude and spring constant, find the kinetic energy at a specified displacement, or the ratio KE:PE there.
Simple circuit diagram with one cell, its internal resistance and an external resistor; find terminal voltage or current, then power dissipated inside the cell.
Two fixed point charges a given distance apart; find where along the line a third charge must be placed so the net force on it is zero.

Rotating system (e.g., a person walking on a turntable or arms folded while spinning); radius/angular speed changes, use angular momentum conservation to find new angular speed or kinetic energy ratio.
Long solenoid with given turns per unit length and current; find the magnetic field at the centre or the field if an iron core of given relative permeability is inserted.
Series LCR circuit with given R, XL and XC (or L, C, f); compute impedance and then the power factor, or average power for a stated rms voltage.
A quantity computed from measured variables (e.g., density from mass and radius); given percentage errors, find the maximum percentage error in the result.
P–V diagram of a cycle made of straight-line segments (e.g., rectangle or triangle); compute net work per cycle and state whether the cycle is clockwise or anticlockwise.

Concave mirror where the object and image have a stated relation (e.g., image distance equals some multiple of object distance or magnification given); use mirror formula plus magnification to solve for focal length.
Body dropped from a height or projected upward near Earth's surface (or between two radii); use energy conservation to find impact speed, ignoring air resistance.
Soap bubble of given radius and surface tension; find the excess pressure inside, or the work done to blow it up from zero radius to the stated radius.
Diagram of Young's double-slit setup with slit separation and screen distance marked; compute fringe width for the given wavelength, or the shift when the whole setup is immersed in a liquid.
Circuit diagram of series–parallel capacitors connected to a battery; reduce the network, find equivalent capacitance and the charge on a specific capacitor.

Point inside or on the surface of a uniform solid sphere; compare gravitational potential/field at centre vs surface and at an interior radius, and select the correct ranking or value (harder conceptual twist).
Flux through a coil changes from one value to another over a stated time interval (or a loop entering/leaving a field region); find the average induced emf using Faraday's law.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slots.brief: Same potential difference accelerates two particles with different mass and charge; find the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths without needing the exact formula values.
Diagram of an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment; using the marked focal lengths, find the magnifying power or the tube length.
Person standing in a lift accelerating up or down with given acceleration; draw the pseudo-force and find the apparent weight (normal reaction) as a fraction or multiple of mg.
A wheel rolls without slipping at a given speed; find the speed or direction of a point on the rim at a specified position (top, side, or at a stated angle).
Circuit diagram: Zener regulator with a series resistor, source voltage and load; compute current through the Zener diode at stated input voltage using the load voltage remaining fixed.
Three coplanar forces in equilibrium, two at stated angles; resolve along axes and find the magnitude of the third force (keep angles standard like 30°, 60°).
Wire is stretched so its length increases by a given percentage or factor (volume constant); find the new resistance or the ratio of new to old resistance.
Source moving towards and then away from a stationary observer at the same speed; find the ratio of the two observed frequencies or compare with the source frequency.
Series LCR circuit at resonance with given R, L, C; express the quality factor Q symbolically and/or compute it, testing the ω0L/R form.
Hydrogen atom electron jumps from a stated higher level to a lower one; find the emitted photon's energy or wavelength using the Bohr energy-level formula.
Circuit diagram of two or three logic gates (e.g., NAND–NAND or mixed gates) with labelled inputs; reduce the circuit and identify the equivalent single gate or output expression.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Light of two stated wavelengths falls on the same metal with given work function; using the photoelectric equation, find the ratio of the maximum kinetic energies of the electrons or the stopping potentials.
Two bodies collide and stick together (e.g., a moving body hits a resting one); apply momentum conservation to find the common velocity and then the kinetic energy lost in the collision.

slots.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slots.brief: Regular polygonal current loop (e.g., square or hexagon) or a two-wire setup; superpose fields from the sides/wires at the centre and find the net magnetic field, possibly using a stated limiting-case check.
Object covers successive parts of a journey with different speeds (e.g., halves of distance at two speeds); compute average speed and see why it is not the arithmetic mean.

slots.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slots.brief: Plane electromagnetic wave of given intensity strikes a surface that is perfectly reflecting or perfectly absorbing; find the radiation pressure or force on the surface, comparing the two cases.
In a double-slit experiment a stated path difference (as a fraction of wavelength) exists at a point; convert to phase difference and find the intensity as a fraction of the maximum.
Given the equation of a travelling wave y(x,t), read off amplitude, wavelength, frequency and wave speed, and state the direction of propagation.
Compare the sign and magnitude of susceptibility and relative permeability for diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic materials; select the correct statement about their field-line behaviour.
Two gases at the same temperature (or the same gas at two temperatures); find the ratio of rms speeds using the v ∝ √(T/m) scaling, no absolute computation needed.
Convert a temperature between two scales (Celsius, Fahrenheit, Kelvin or a made-up linear scale) using the standard linear-conversion relation.
Wire of given length, cross-sectional area (or radius) and Young's modulus under a known load; compute the elongation or the stress–strain pair, all from Y = (F/A)/(ΔL/L).
Alkyl halide undergoes dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH, then the alkene is treated with HBr in absence of peroxide; ask for the major final product considering Markovnikov addition.
Given mass of a known nonelectrolyte dissolved in a solvent mass and Kf, compute the freezing point of the solution.
Given initial amount and fraction remaining after a time, use number of half-lives to find the half-life or the time required.
Identify which listed vitamin is fat-soluble / match a vitamin with its deficiency disease; keep it to single-fact recall.
Which statement about ozone-depleting substances / mechanism of Cl radical catalysed ozone decomposition is correct; simple fact-check statements.
Compare cloudiness appearance time for a primary, secondary and tertiary alcohol with Lucas reagent; ask which reacts immediately and why.
Give a Fischer projection of a two-chiral-centre molecule in the figure; ask students to rank/identify the correct R/S assignment and enantiomer/diastereomer relation among drawn structures.
State the geometry and hybridisation of XeF4 (square planar) among options; simple structure identification.
Mixture of two non-reacting gases in a vessel: given masses and molar masses, find total pressure at a given temperature using partial pressures and PV = nRT.
Rank a set of cyclic/acyclic species (including an antiaromatic ion and an aromatic ion) by stability using Hückel's rule.
Compare [Fe(CN)6]4− and [Fe(H2O)6]2+ for hybridisation and magnetic nature (diamagnetic vs paramagnetic); pick the correct pairing.
Show an asymmetric ether (figure) treated with excess HI; identify both products and note why the cleavage occurs at the bond giving the stable carbocation/SN1 path.
Four options giving electron gain enthalpy orders across halogens/chalcogens/N–O pair; pick the incorrect one, testing the Cl > F exception and S > O anomaly.
Use limiting molar conductivities of two known strong electrolytes to compute Λ°m of a third (e.g., acetic acid from HCl, NaCl, CH3COONa).
Ratio of Bohr radii or energies of He+ vs H for the same n, or energy of an n-th level of a hydrogen-like ion; single scaling formula.
Identify shapes of simple species like ClF3 / SO2 / NH3 from VSEPR lone-pair counting; pick correct shape set from options.
Given spin-only magnetic moment of a transition metal ion, back-calculate the number of unpaired electrons and identify the metal ion.
Convert aniline to a target substituted arene (figure shows starting amine and product, e.g., to m-bromophenol); choose the correct reagent sequence involving diazotisation and substitution.
Products and structures on hydrolysis of PCl5 / SiCl4 / NCl3 with balanced outcomes; ask which hydrolysis gives a specific oxide acid set — high-difficulty, multi-product reasoning.

slots.subtopic: Diagonal relationship of Li and Mg
slots.brief: Which properties of Li resemble Mg rather than other alkali metals (nitride formation, carbonate decomposition); pick the correct set of shared properties.
For a combustion reaction with given ΔU, compute ΔH using Δng of gases; direct substitution with R in appropriate units.
Ask which compound is obtained when a Grignard reagent reacts with a specified substrate (water/CO2/methanol) or which reagent destroys a Grignard reagent; simple product identification.
Which of the given ions is colourless in aqueous solution (d0 or d10 ion like Cu+/Zn2+/Sc3+); single-concept recall.
Identify which aldehyde undergoes Cannizzaro reaction and why (no α-hydrogen); could include a mild computation of the mole ratio of alcohol to acid formed.
For an exothermic equilibrium like N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, predict the effect of increasing pressure/temperature/addition of inert gas at constant volume on yield.
Give log(x/m) vs log P data/plot; extract the slope and intercept, state what slope = 1 means, and interpret adsorption behaviour — includes a subtle point about saturation limiting the isotherm.
Compare de Broglie wavelength of an electron vs an alpha particle accelerated through the same potential difference (or same kinetic energy); derive the ratio from mass and charge.
Which statements about Hess's law / state functions / enthalpy being path independent are correct; simple true-false style multi-statement option.
Rank given ligands (CN−, F−, H2O, I−) by crystal field splitting strength using the spectrochemical series; straightforward ordering.
In a spinel-like or NaCl-type arrangement, determine the fraction of octahedral voids occupied or the formula of the compound given occupancy.
Rank C–O bond lengths / bond orders in species like CO, CO2, CO3^2−, HCOOH using resonance structures and formal bond order counting.
Draw an alkene (figure, e.g., a cyclic diene) and ask for the dicarbonyl product(s) after ozonolysis with Zn/H2O; requires identifying both cleavage sites.
For PCl5 ⇌ PCl3 + Cl2 at given total pressure and α, set up ICE table and compute Kp; single-equation numerical.
Rank acidity of terminal alkyne vs alkene vs alkane, or identify which alkynyl anion forms with NaNH2; conceptual comparison with reagent recognition.
Rank a set of given radicals (benzylic, allylic, tertiary, methyl) by stability; straightforward compare-and-rank with resonance reasoning.
Evaluate statements on NH3, PH3, AsH3 regarding thermal stability, reducing character and bond angle trends down the group; pick the correct combination.
Identify which hydride is ionic / which reacts with water liberating H2; simple classification of NaH, CH4, HCl type species.
Match/use of artificial sweeteners (aspartame, sucralose, alitame, saccharin) — identify the sweetener usable by a phenylketonuria patient or match sweetener to property/use.
Compare change in conductivity and molar conductivity with dilution for strong vs weak electrolyte; pick the correct trend explanation.
Given percentage composition of an organic compound and molar mass, find the molecular formula; simple ratio simplification to empirical formula.

slots.subtopic: Active to Passive Voice – present perfect/continuous tenses
slots.brief: Ask the student to pick the correct passive transformation of a present perfect sentence (e.g., 'has completed'); distractors with wrong auxiliary or participle forms.

slots.subtopic: Sentence rearrangement (PQRS) – argumentative paragraph with fixed first and last sentences
slots.brief: Give a fixed opening and closing sentence on an abstract topic (e.g., technology and society) with four jumbled middle sentences P–Q–R–S that must be ordered using pronoun and connector clues; hard because of subtle linkages.
Sentence with a collective/indefinite subject (e.g., 'each of the players') where the verb disagrees; one part contains the error, other parts are clean.
Blank for the correct preposition in a fixed expression (e.g., 'comply ___', 'preface ___'); distractors are common near-miss prepositions.

slots.subtopic: Sentence rearrangement – identify the first sentence
slots.brief: Four jumbled short sentences of a simple narrative/event; the student must identify which sentence logically opens the passage (e.g., the one introducing the setting/person without pronoun reference).
Sentence using a future tense in a 'when/after/until' clause incorrectly (e.g., 'when he will arrive'); student must choose the corrected simple-present version.

Sentence testing gerund form after a preposition (e.g., 'insisted on going'); design it so the sentence is actually correct – 'No error' is the right option, with distractor parts tempting misidentification.
Fill the blank in an everyday sentence with the correct phrasal verb (e.g., 'call off / call up / call for') based on context meaning.
Give a moderately common descriptive adjective (e.g., 'arduous') in a short context sentence; options are near-synonyms, only one precise match.
Single-blank sentence where the surrounding context (e.g., 'despite his illness, he remained ___') fixes the meaning; four plausible adjectives, one fits.
Ask for the antonym of a straightforward abstract word (e.g., 'frugal' or 'candid'); options include a wrong-direction synonym as a trap.
Analogy pair such as 'Benevolent : Kind :: ? : ?' where the student picks the pair with the same synonym-intensity or degree relationship; distractors shift the relationship type.
Give an action verb (e.g., 'embellish' or 'mitigate') in a one-line context and ask for the closest meaning from four options; distractors are loosely related but imprecise.
Short family description; ask how many members are male or how many cousins a named person has.
Four word pairs where three share a hidden relationship (e.g., product-place or worker-tool); pick the pair that breaks the pattern.
A word is coded by shifting each letter a fixed but non-uniform rule (e.g., alternate +1/+2); apply the same rule to a new word.
Pair like CDF : HIK where a consistent shift maps one to the other; find the analogous fourth term.
Arrange four similar-spelled words as in a dictionary and identify which comes second or last.
Mixed letter-number series where each block follows separate patterns; find the missing next block.
Two statements with overlapping categories; evaluate three conclusions including a possibility case and an either-or pair.
Draw balls/cards without replacement; ask for probability of a described composition (e.g. all same colour or exactly one of a kind); simple fraction counting.
Given sum of first n terms and a condition on nth term, find first term and common difference; moderate algebra.
Definite integral of a function symmetric about midpoint (f(a+b−x) relation) combined with a standard result like ∫dx/(1+x²) or log form; use symmetry to simplify.
Find the domain of a composite function combining a square root and a logarithm; intersect conditions.
Given a quadratic, evaluate an expression symmetric in roots such as α³ + β³ or 1/α² + 1/β² using Vieta's relations.
Piecewise function with a, b parameters; find values making it continuous at the junction (possibly also matching one-sided limits).
Small data set; compute mean deviation about the mean (or median) — table-free direct computation with clean numbers.
Sum an arithmetico-geometric series to n terms (or infinity) such as Σ n xⁿ; use the shift-and-subtract method; moderately demanding algebra.
Determinant whose entries are row sums/column expressions; show it equals a product of linear factors using row/column operations.
Evaluate |(1+i)/(something)|-type expression using |z₁/z₂| = |z₁|/|z₂|; quick computation, no heavy algebra.
Find the equation of the tangent (or normal) to a curve given implicitly or with an inverse trig form at a given point; moderate slope computation.
Evaluate an expression like tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y or a sin/tan⁻¹ combination reduced via the addition identity; straightforward.
Given an ellipse (or foci + a vertex), find eccentricity or foci using b² = a²(1−e²); single-formula application.
Limit of the form (1 − cos kx)/x² or sin(ax)/sin(bx) using standard trig limits; easy substitution after simplification.
Count 3-digit (or 4-digit) numbers from given digits with a simple restriction (odd/even, no repetition, divisibility by 5); basic case split.
Two/three-set problem with |A∩B|, |A∪B| given; find a cardinality via inclusion–exclusion; easy plug-in.
Solve dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) with a non-obvious P(x) (e.g. involving 1/x or trig) using integrating factor; find particular solution given y(0).
Two-population problem (e.g. machines/balls from bags); given test/result probabilities, compute posterior probability the item came from a given source; multi-step Bayes.
Find the range of a rational function like (x²+ax+b)/(quadratic) by setting y = f(x) and imposing discriminant ≥ 0; hard — include a subtle domain exclusion.
Solve an equation reducible to a single trig function (e.g. via factorising sin/cos) and state the general solution set; standard.

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: Find the image of a given point in a given line; use foot-of-perpendicular then reflection; moderate two-step computation.
Indefinite integral requiring integration by parts, possibly applied twice or with the 'ILATE' trick of adding the same integral to both sides.
At-least-k or exactly-k successes problem (coins/dice/items defective); compute using binomial probabilities; clean numbers.
Definite integral where a substitution like x = a sinθ or t = √x collapses it; easy once the right substitution is spotted.
Two lines in vector/cartesian form; compute shortest distance via the scalar triple product formula; moderate arithmetic.
Simplify or evaluate an expression using sum-to-product and double-angle identities, e.g. prove/evaluate a compound angle expression; moderate.
Line touches a circle (or circle touches axes/another circle); use distance from centre = radius to find an unknown parameter; easy.
For a small matrix A, compute Aⁿ or an expression like A³ − 3A² + I; exploit a pattern or Cayley–Hamilton relation; moderate.
Find the constant (x-free) term in an expansion such as (xᵖ + 1/x^q)ⁿ or a product of two binomials; set exponent of x to zero via general term.
Area enclosed between a parabola and a line (or two curves) needing intersection points and a signed-integral split; moderately hard with clean limits.
Differentiate an inverse trig composite, e.g. tan⁻¹(something) or sin⁻¹(2x/(1+x²)); apply chain rule with the standard derivative formula.
Domain of √(simple quadratic or linear condition); require the radicand ≥ 0 — one inequality, quick answer.
Given a line by two points, find its direction cosines; direct formula with normalization — very easy.
Data transformed as y = ax + b; state/compute the new variance and mean using transformation properties; conceptual with one small computation.
Given a condition (focus, or vertex + directrix), construct the equation of the parabola; moderate — may need completing the square or axis identification.
Compute [a b c] for given vectors or show coplanarity/volume via determinant; moderate arithmetic, possibly with a parameter to find.
Hard: given |z−z₁| = k|z−z₂| or argument condition, find the locus (circle/line) and then a parameter (radius, centre, min |z|) — multi-step with conjugate manipulation.
Find the interval on which a simple polynomial or basic function is increasing; compute f′(x) and check sign — very easy.
Given compound statements with ∧, ∨, ~, check which option is logically equivalent (or write the negation of an implication); use De Morgan / conditional rules.
Hard: simplify/evaluate an expression like a×(b×c) + b×(c×a) or prove a Jacobi-identity style relation; requires careful identity use and possibly given magnitudes/angles.
Indefinite integral of the form ∫dx/(a sin x + b cos x) or ∫(sin/cos power mix) via t = tan(x/2) or a simple substitution; easy with the right trick.
Arrange letters of a word (with repetition) so that vowels come together or two letters never adjacent; standard block/complement method — easy-moderate.
Two lines given in general form (or reduce them to parallel form) and find the distance between them; direct formula, careful with coefficients.
System of 3 equations in 3 unknowns with a parameter; find values of the parameter for which the system has no solution / infinitely many; compare Δ with Δx, Δy, Δz — hard.
Solve dy/dx = f(y/x) type homogeneous equation using y = vx; end with a general solution in log form; standard moderate solve.
